D_policy_objective: Regulates the classification, segregation, packaging, pre-treatment, storage, transport, treatment and final disposal of biomedical waste generated by health facilities (hospitals, clinics, laboratories), veterinary structures, industrial producers of biomedical products, and research activities, and sets accreditation/traceability obligations for all actors in the biomedical-waste chain (Rapport de présentation; Art. 1-2). Its principal objective is protecting health workers, patients, waste handlers and the public from infection, injury and toxic exposure, and the environment from contamination -- not plastics regulation as such. However, Art. 3 (definitions) and Art. 4 (classification) explicitly and directly name plastics: 'recyclage' is defined with reference to 'papier, plastique', and the decree creates a dedicated waste category, 'déchets recyclables', defined as 'les déchets plastiques tels que les flacons de sérum, d'eau de javel, le matériel en verre, les contenants sous pression' -- i.e. the very common plastic packaging of healthcare consumables (serum/IV-fluid bottles, bleach/disinfectant bottles, pressurised containers). Art. 11.1 then directs that this plastic/recyclable waste stream follow the general household-waste pathway rather than incineration or burial, making this decree a genuine (if narrowly sector-bound) plastics-waste-management instrument for the healthcare sector, consistent with the task brief's framing: 'Relevant to plastics waste management but limited to healthcare.'
H_policy_type_justification: A presidential decree: 'Décrète :' issued by 'Le Président de la République' (Abdoulaye Wade), countersigned by the Prime Minister (Cheikh Hadjibou Soumaré), 'Fait à Dakar, le 18 août 2008.' It is issued by the executive branch under existing legislation (citing, among others, Loi n° 2001-01 portant Code de l'Environnement and the Code de l'Hygiène) rather than being itself an Act adopted by the National Assembly -> sub-legislative regulation, coded 0.75 per Rule 6.
J_policy_sectors_list: health, veterinary, industry, research, waste management, environment, local government/municipalities, chemicals, transport
R_instrument_description: Art. 5: 'Toute personne physique ou morale, qui produit ou détient des déchets biomédicaux, en assure elle-même l'élimination ou le recyclage ou les fait éliminer ou recycler auprès des entreprises agréées par le Ministre chargé de la santé.' A mandatory producer/holder duty to ensure elimination or recycling of biomedical waste -- including the plastic waste stream defined at Art. 4 -- either directly or via Ministry-approved companies.
U_instrument_implementation_text: Authority: approved companies are 'agréées par le Ministre chargé de la santé' (+0.25). Monitoring: Art. 20 requires 'les producteurs et les opérateurs' (which includes the persons targeted by Art. 5) to register their waste and ensure its traceability -- a data-collection requirement directly applicable to this duty (+0.25). Unconditional: the duty applies to 'toute personne physique ou morale' with no exemption identified (+0.25). Enforcement: no explicit fine/sanction was identified that is clearly triggered by a producer's (as opposed to an accredited operator's) breach of this specific duty -- not awarded, see the accreditation-sanctions row below for the operator-side enforcement mechanism.
W_comments: This is the general producer-responsibility duty for biomedical waste, functionally analogous to the general waste-elimination duties coded elsewhere in this series for the Code de l'Environnement, but here explicitly extending to the sector-specific 'déchets plastiques' category defined at Art. 4.

R_instrument_description: Art. 6: 'Tout déchet issu des activités médicales, pharmaceutiques, vétérinaires ou de recherche, est trié au niveau du lieu même de production et mis dans le circuit spécifique dédié à cette catégorie en fonction de la classification. R_instrument_description: Art. 11(1): treatment-stream assignment by waste category -- 'les déchets assimilés aux ordures ménagères, de même que les déchets recyclables, suivent la filière des déchets ménagers'; infectious/potentially infectious waste is incinerated, buried, or sterilised/shredded (Art. 11(2)); anatomical waste is buried or incinerated (Art. 11(3)); sharps are incinerated, buried or sterilised/shredded (Art. 11(4)); pharmaceutical waste follows a Ministry-specific procedure or is returned to the pharmacy (Art. 11(5)); special/chemical waste undergoes substance-specific treatment, and radioactive waste follows the separate radiation-protection legal regime (Art. 11(6)).
U_instrument_implementation_text: Authority: falls under the Minister chargé de la Santé's execution responsibility (Art. 22), with pharmaceutical-waste procedures specifically elaborated 'par le Ministère chargé de la santé' (Art. 11(5)) (+0.25). Unconditional: the treatment-stream table 's'établit comme suit' is a definitive, mandatory assignment with no exemption identified (+0.25). Enforcement/Monitoring: no dedicated fine or inspection mechanism specific to mis-assignment between treatment streams was identified -- not awarded.
W_comments: The single most directly plastics-relevant operative provision in the decree: by directing 'déchets recyclables' (i.e. the plastic bottles/containers defined at Art. 4) into 'la filière des déchets ménagers' rather than incineration or landfill, this instrument links healthcare plastic waste into the general municipal solid-waste/recycling system already coded elsewhere in this series (e.g. Loi n° 2023-15, Art. 85-90; Loi n° 2001-01, Art. L32-L36).

R_instrument_description: Art. 12: 'L'installation et le fonctionnement d'un incinérateur doivent être conformes à la réglementation en vigueur, notamment aux prescriptions édictées dans le dossier des installations classées. La température minimale d'incinération requise est de 800° C. Les résidus de l'incinération doivent faire l'objet d'un enfouissement hygiénique.' A technology/performance standard for biomedical-waste incinerators, cross-referencing the classified-installations (ICPE) regime and setting a minimum operating temperature and mandatory hygienic burial of ash residues.
U_instrument_implementation_text: Authority: incinerators fall under the classified-installations ('installations classées') permitting authority (Ministère chargé de l'Environnement), already coded in detail elsewhere in this series (+0.25). Unconditional: the 800°C minimum temperature and mandatory hygienic ash burial are stated categorically with no exemption identified (+0.25). Enforcement/Monitoring: no incinerator-specific fine or inspection mechanism is stated within this decree itself (as distinct from the general ICPE inspection/enforcement regime coded separately for Décret n° 2001-282, which is not explicitly cross-referenced by article number here) -- not awarded to avoid double-counting evidence coded under a different policy entry.
W_comments: Directly relevant to plastic-containing biomedical waste (e.g. PPE, syringes, IV tubing) that is incinerated rather than recycled: sets the minimum technical standard for how that combustion must occur. Cross-reference: the ICPE permitting/enforcement apparatus this article invokes is coded in full under Décret n° 2001-282 and Loi n° 2023-15 elsewhere in this series.

Enforcement: 'L'agrément est retiré...ou...une suspension temporaire de 1 à 12 mois' (Art. 21) -- an explicit sanction (+0.25). Monitoring: withdrawal/suspension decisions are explicitly based on findings 'après inspection' (Art. 21) (+0.25). Unconditional: not awarded -- the advisory commission's composition and mission depend on a further ministerial order not yet specified within this decree's own text (Art. 15), and sanctions are conditioned on inspection findings rather than automatic.
W_comments: The accreditation-plus-sanctions regime is the decree's central enforcement backbone for every operator handling the plastic/recyclable waste stream, alongside all other biomedical-waste categories. In-force test (Rule 12): the core accreditation duty (Art. 14, 'doit obtenir') and the sanctions power (Art. 21, 'est retiré') are mandatory and self-executing, so S=1, even though the advisory commission's specific composition (Art. 15) remains an enabling power pending a further order.

D_policy_objective: Regulates the classification, segregation, packaging, pre-treatment, storage, transport, treatment and final disposal of biomedical waste generated by health facilities (hospitals, clinics, laboratories), veterinary structures, industrial producers of biomedical products, and research activities, and sets accreditation/traceability obligations for all actors in the biomedical-waste chain (Rapport de présentation; Art. 1-2). Its principal objective is protecting health workers, patients, waste handlers and the public from infection, injury and toxic exposure, and the environment from contamination -- not plastics regulation as such. However, Art. 3 (definitions) and Art. 4 (classification) explicitly and directly name plastics: 'recyclage' is defined with reference to 'papier, plastique', and the decree creates a dedicated waste category, 'déchets recyclables', defined as 'les déchets plastiques tels que les flacons de sérum, d'eau de javel, le matériel en verre, les contenants sous pression' -- i.e. the very common plastic packaging of healthcare consumables (serum/IV-fluid bottles, bleach/disinfectant bottles, pressurised containers). Art. 11.1 then directs that this plastic/recyclable waste stream follow the general household-waste pathway rather than incineration or burial, making this decree a genuine (if narrowly sector-bound) plastics-waste-management instrument for the healthcare sector, consistent with the task brief's framing: 'Relevant to plastics waste management but limited to healthcare.'
H_policy_type_justification: A presidential decree: 'Décrète :' issued by 'Le Président de la République' (Abdoulaye Wade), countersigned by the Prime Minister (Cheikh Hadjibou Soumaré), 'Fait à Dakar, le 18 août 2008.' It is issued by the executive branch under existing legislation (citing, among others, Loi n° 2001-01 portant Code de l'Environnement and the Code de l'Hygiène) rather than being itself an Act adopted by the National Assembly -> sub-legislative regulation, coded 0.75 per Rule 6.

R_instrument_description: Art. 20: 'Les producteurs et les opérateurs sont tenus d'enregistrer leurs déchets et d'en assurer la traçabilité.' A mandatory record-keeping and traceability duty imposed on both waste producers and operators across the whole biomedical-waste chain, including the plastic/recyclable stream.
U_instrument_implementation_text: Authority: falls under the Minister chargé de la Santé's general execution responsibility (Art. 22) (+0.25). Monitoring: this instrument is itself an explicit data-collection requirement -- 'enregistrer leurs déchets et...assurer la traçabilité' (+0.25). Unconditional: applies to 'les producteurs et les opérateurs' generally, with no exemption identified (+0.25). Enforcement: no specific penalty distinct from the general accreditation-based sanctions (coded separately above) is stated for a traceability failure as such -- not awarded here to avoid double counting.
W_comments: A cross-cutting monitoring/data-collection instrument applicable to every waste category and every actor coded in this table.

R_instrument_description: Art. 9: 'Le stockage des déchets conditionnés, avant traitement se fait dans un local aéré et sécurisé. Le local doit être facilement décontaminable, régulièrement décontaminé (une fois par semaine au moins) de capacité suffisante et accessible au ramassage. Enforcement: no storage-specific fine is stated distinct from the general accreditation-based sanctions regime -- not awarded here to avoid double counting.
W_comments: Applies to the plastic/recyclable waste stream during the pre-treatment storage window alongside all other biomedical-waste categories.
